DryRun.description: Validate the whole file and roll back.
DryRun.name: dry_run

From.description: Inclusive lower bound, YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339.
From.name: from

Lang.description: Overrides Accept-Language. Falls back to the store's default language when unsupported.
Lang.name: lang

Offset.description: How many records to skip. Ignored when `page` is also given.
Offset.name: offset

PageNumber.description: The page to return, counting from 1. An alternative to `offset` — `?limit=20&page=3` is the same window as `?limit=20&offset=40`. When both are sent, `page` wins: it is the more specific intent.
PageNumber.name: page

AuthResponse.description: A session token and the operator it belongs to.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state.

Unauthorized.description: A valid admin token is required.

track_url.description: Where the customer follows the parcel, with the number already in it. Absent when the carrier has no URL that takes the number as a parameter — a client should then show the number without a link rather than a link that fails.

id.description: The cart's opaque token, and the only credential involved.

available.description: -1 when the variant does not track inventory.

price_changed.description: The live price differs from the snapshot, so checkout will refuse until the shopper confirms.

Category.description: A node in the product taxonomy. Not a collection: a collection is a curated list a product can be on six of, while a category answers "what kind of thing is this", which has exactly one answer — which is what a feed, a tax rule and a shipping profile all need to key off.

children.description: Populated by the nested listing only. A flat listing omits it, so the same rows never appear twice in one response.

depth.description: 0 for a root. Present so a flat listing can be indented without the client rebuilding the tree.

full_name.description: The ancestry joined for display. Computed on read, never stored: a stored path would need rewriting across a whole subtree on every rename, and the first missed rewrite is a lie nothing ever finds.

position.description: Orders a category against its siblings.

metadata.description: The `attributes` key is the list of fields this category asks of a product, as `{key, label, choices}`, inherited by everything beneath it.

parent_id.description: Null files the category at the root. The tree is capped at 8 deep.

slug.description: Derived from the title when absent.

CategoryPage.description: A category with the active products filed under it or under anything beneath it. Descendants are included because that is what the operator means: someone who picks "Apparel" wants the shirts too.

CategoryPatch.description: Only the keys present are written. Moving a category re-parents its whole subtree, so the depth cap and the cycle check apply to the move.

metadata.description: The `attributes` key is the list of fields this category asks of a product, as `{key, label, choices}`, inherited by everything beneath it.

parent_id.description: Null files the category at the root. The tree is capped at 8 deep.

slug.description: Derived from the title when absent.

payment_data.description: Passed through to the payment provider, so a gateway can receive what it needs without this body growing a field per integration.

return_url.description: Where a redirect-flow gateway sends the shopper back to.

Collection.description: A named, hand-curated grouping of products. Rule-based ("smart") collections are deliberately absent: they need a query language, and what a catalog this size uses is a list somebody picked.

position.description: Orders collections against each other — a navigation menu, not the order of products inside one.

slug.description: Derived from the title when omitted, exactly as a product's is.

CollectionPage.description: A collection with the active products in it. One request rather than two, because there is no useful moment at which a storefront has the collection but not its contents.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Every failure uses this shape, whatever endpoint produced it.

details.description: Structured detail, such as per-line checkout conflicts.

FulfillmentPatch.description: Only the keys present are written. Changing the tracking number re-identifies the carrier, because the stored one described the old number; an explicit `carrier` in the same request wins over that.

carrier.description: A code from GET /api/admin/carriers, or empty.

ListMeta.description: Accompanies every paginated collection. Both coordinate systems are reported: `offset` for a client walking a cursor, and `page` for a UI drawing "3 of 12". The page fields are derived from the offset, so the two can never disagree.

page.description: The page this window falls in, counting from 1.

total.description: Matching records in the whole collection, not just this page.

total_pages.description: Pages at this limit. Zero when nothing matched.

Media.description: One file in the store-wide library. Note what is absent: the storage key is an internal handle and is never serialized.

filename.description: The name it was uploaded under, kept for display only — never used as a path.

url.description: Where the file is readable. Site-relative for files this store holds.

Money.description: An integer count of the currency's minor unit, plus the currency. Never a float, because binary floating point cannot represent 0.10; never a formatted string, because the decimal places belong to the currency and the symbol belongs to the reader's locale.

OptionChange.description: What replacing the matrix actually did, so an operator is told rather than left to discover it.

Order.description: An immutable record of a sale. Its lines and customer details are snapshots, so a historical order stays readable after the catalog moves on.

access_token.description: Returned once, at checkout. It is how a guest reads their own order back.

OrderPatch.description:
Corrects what was recorded about an order: who it is for, and how it was paid for. Only the keys present are written.

It deliberately cannot reach status, payment status, totals or line items. Each of those is a state change with consequences — stock, events, money — and each already has an operation that performs them properly. This is for the fields somebody typed.

email.description: Required to be non-empty: it is how the customer hears about the order.

payment_provider.description: A method installed in this build. It may be changed while nothing has been refunded — an order taken as cash on delivery and actually settled by transfer should say so — but not after, where the money went out through the provider currently on the order.

payment_reference.description: The transaction or receipt number the money is reconciled against.

kind.description: `none` means nothing further is needed — cash on delivery.

Product.description: The merchandising concept. What a shopper actually buys is a variant.

category.description: Absent when the product is uncategorised, which is a normal state for a draft rather than an error.

collections.description: Carried on every product read, so membership renders without a request per product.

metadata.description: Where a module attaches its own data, under its own key.

product_type.description: Free text an operator groups and filters by, such as "Shirt".

seo_title.description: The storefront's <title>. Empty means derive it from the title — whether and how is the storefront's call.

tags.description: Normalised on write: trimmed, de-duplicated case-insensitively, and sorted. Case is preserved, but two spellings of one tag are one tag.

ProductCategory.description: The trimmed category carried on a product: enough to render a breadcrumb and link to it.

ProductCollection.description: The trimmed collection carried on a product: enough to render a chip and link to it, and no more.

category_id.description: The category to file the product under. Omit for uncategorised.

sku.description: Shorthand for a product with no options; send with price_minor instead of variants.

slug.description: Derived from the title when omitted.

tags.description: Stored normalised — trimmed, de-duplicated case-insensitively and sorted — so the order they arrive in does not become part of the record.

variant_id.description: Set when the file belongs to one variant rather than the whole product.

ProductOption.description: One axis of choice, such as Size.

Superuser.description: An admin-panel operator. Note what is absent: no password hash is ever serialized.

Variant.description: The sellable unit: SKU, price and stock live here, and cart and order lines reference it. A product with no options still has exactly one.

continue_selling.description: Take the order when the count has run out, instead of refusing it.

cost.description: What the item cost this store, for margin reporting. Absent means nobody has recorded a cost — which is not the same as a cost of zero, and the difference matters: a zero would report a 100% margin on something nobody has costed. A storefront never sees this.

image.description: Absent when the variant has not nominated one, which is the normal case for most variants.

origin_country.description: Where the item was made, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

taxable.description: Whether tax applies to this variant. True for almost everything, and the safe default to be wrong about: tax charged in error is refundable, tax not charged is not. It sits on the variant rather than the product because a gift card and a shirt can share a product's shape and not its tax treatment.

weight.description: The same mass rendered for display, so a client that only shows it need not know that a pound is 453.59237 g.

weight_grams.description: The canonical stored weight. Whole grams, because that is the resolution a carrier API is given and a float that cannot represent 0.1 exactly would eventually produce a total that does not add up.

weight_unit.description: How the weight should be read, exactly as a currency code says how an amount should be read. The grams are the fact; the unit is presentation, kept so an operator who typed 2.5 kg sees 2.5 kg again and not 2500 g.

VariantImage.description: The one of its product's images a variant nominates — what a storefront swaps to when a shopper picks a colour. A variant never owns a file; it points at one the product already shows, so the same picture is stored once.

continue_selling.description: Take the order when the count has run out, instead of refusing it.

cost_minor.description: Cost in the store's minor units. Send null to clear a recorded cost.

options.description: The value chosen on each of the product's axes, in any order.

origin_country.description: Where the item was made, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

weight.description: The weight in `weight_unit`, converted server-side. Sent together with the unit this is a form's shape; when both this and `weight_grams` arrive, this one wins — a caller that computed grams itself and then also sent a value contradicted itself, and the human-entered number is the one a person can check.

weight_grams.description: The weight in grams. The API's shape; a form should send `weight` and `weight_unit` instead.

adminToken.description: Either a static token from Config.AdminTokens — the right credential for a script, since it has no session and no expiry — or a superuser session token from /api/admin/auth-with-password, which is the right credential for a person. Both arrive the same way and satisfy the same middleware.

info.description:
A small, composable commerce engine for Go.

Money is always an integer count of the currency's minor unit plus its code — never a float, never a formatted string. The number of decimal places belongs to the currency (USD has 2, JPY has 0, KWD has 3) and formatting belongs to the client.

Every response is `{"data": ...}` or `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`. Every collection paginates.

Guest checkout is permanent: a shopper needs a cart token and an email, never an account.
info.title: gocommerce

post.description: The panel calls this on boot to turn a stored token back into an identity, and to learn that a token has expired without waiting for a real request to fail. The old token is revoked. A static admin token is not a session and gets a 400.
post.summary: Exchange a session for a fresh one

get.description: Public, because it has to answer before anyone can hold a credential. The panel calls it first so a fresh database offers to create the first superuser instead of presenting a login form nobody could satisfy.

token_auth.description: A static admin token would also be accepted.

get.summary: Whether this installation has an operator yet

post.description: Returns a session token to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Wrong password and unknown operator give the identical 400, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover who has an account. Repeated failures from one address are throttled.

identity.description: The operator's email. Named `identity` for PocketBase compatibility; `email` is accepted as a synonym.

post.summary: Sign in with an email and a password

get.description:
Without `tracking`, every carrier the engine can name. With it, the ones whose numbering the number fits, best first.

That is a list rather than a verdict on purpose. A tracking number is not self-describing: several carriers issue bare ten- to fourteen-digit numbers, so a twelve-digit number is genuinely ambiguous. Where a number carries something distinctive — UPS's `1Z`, the S10 standard's country suffix, DHL's `JJD` — the list has one entry and a client can fill the field in. Where it does not, the operator picks. Guessing would hand the customer a tracking link that goes nowhere, which reads as the shop having lost their parcel.

parameters.description: Return only the carriers this number could belong to.
parameters.name: tracking

get.summary: Carriers, or the ones a tracking number could belong to

get.description: Three shapes from one route. `?q=` searches the whole tree and answers with a bounded flat set of paths, which is the normal way to work once a full taxonomy is imported. `?parent=root` or `?parent={id}` returns one level, the shape a browsable picker asks for, bounded by construction. Neither, and the whole tree comes back, but only while it is small enough to send honestly: past that the response is a bounded slice whose `meta.total` reports the real size, so a client that compares the two can see it holds only a part and switch to searching.

parameters.description: `root`, or a category id: return that node's direct children only.
parameters.name: parent

parameters.description: Depth-first flat list instead of nested children.
parameters.name: flat

200.description: Categories. `meta.total` is the real size of the tree, which can exceed what was sent.

get.summary: List, search or browse the tree

delete.description: Refused while anything still points at it, whether a subcategory or a product filed under it. Deleting a branch is not a way to lose what was in it, so the references have to be moved first.

get.description: The chain from the root down to this category, the category itself last. A client that holds one category and needs what the whole branch says about it cannot get there from the listing — a store carrying a full taxonomy has thousands of categories and the listing sends a page — so the chain is asked for by id. Each node carries its metadata, which is where a category declares the fields it asks of a product. An unknown id comes back as an empty list rather than a 404: it is a category deleted while somebody had the product open.
get.summary: The branch a category sits on, root first

get.description: Every collection, including the empty ones the public listing hides.

200.description: A page of collections, ordered by position then id.

delete.description: The products in it survive. A collection groups products, it does not own them, so deleting "Summer sale" must not delete the summer stock — only the membership rows go.

patch.description: Every field is optional; an omitted field is left alone.

post.description: Books a shipment and moves the order to shipped. With the built-in `manual` provider an operator packs the box and types the tracking number; a carrier module reads `meta` for its own options, such as courier choice or pickup slot.

get.description: One row per order line, with the order's columns repeated — the shape an accountant's pivot table wants.
One row per variant. Cells beginning with =, +, - or @ are prefixed with an apostrophe, because a spreadsheet executes those on open; import strips exactly one back, so the round trip stays lossless.

delete.description:
The order follows it. "Shipped" was true because that record existed, so removing the last one that says so puts the order back to confirmed — leaving it shipped with nothing shipping it would be a state no operation could explain and no operator could correct.

Refused on a delivered order: a parcel somebody received is not a record to erase, and undoing the delivery first is the operation that says so.

Returns the order, whose status may have moved with the shipment.
delete.summary: Remove a shipment recorded in error

patch.description: Typing a tracking number is the one step of shipping a parcel nobody else checks, so it is the one that gets mistyped. This changes what was recorded about the shipment and nothing about the order: the parcel left either way, and correcting the number is not un-shipping it.

post.description: For migrating from another platform. It does not touch inventory — those stock movements happened on the old system — and it fires no events unless `fire_events` is set, because importing five thousand orders must not send five thousand confirmation emails. An order whose number already exists is skipped, so re-importing an export is a no-op.

Upserts by SKU. Rows for one product must be contiguous — which is what export produces — so a large file streams instead of being held in memory. A bad row is reported with its line number and never aborts the file.
Public only while no superuser exists; afterwards it is 409 for everyone. This is the one-time window that lets a fresh install become usable without shell access.

get.summary: Variants at or below a stock threshold

get.description: Newest first, which is what "select existing" wants: the file you just uploaded is usually the one you want. Every filter narrows in the store, so a page of results is a page of the whole library rather than of what a client already holds.

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the filename, the alt text or the URL. A substring rather than full text, because a library is names, not prose.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: `used` is media at least one product displays; `unused` is the orphans, which is the reason the filter exists. Anything else is a 400 rather than an ignored filter.
parameters.name: usage

parameters.description: Only media the given product displays.
parameters.name: product_id

parameters.description: Lower bound on file size. Media recorded by URL reports zero bytes, so any lower bound excludes it.
parameters.name: min_bytes

parameters.description: Upper bound on file size. Omit for no upper bound — which is what makes "over 5 MB" expressible without a sentinel value.
parameters.name: max_bytes

post.description: A multipart form with a `file` field, and optionally `alt`. Accepts images, video and 3D models (glb, gltf, usdz); anything else is refused, because an upload is served back from this origin and a document or script there would be a stored-XSS vector. The uploaded filename is never used as a path — it is kept for display only. Returns 501 when the store has nowhere to put files (neither Config.MediaDir nor Config.MediaStore is set); the library still records media by URL in that case.

501.description: This store has nowhere to put uploads.

post.description: Adds a library entry for a file this store does not hold. No storage key is recorded, so deleting it only ever removes the row — nothing is ever deleted from someone else's server.

delete.description: Refused with 409 while any product still displays it — deleting a file six products show should be a decision, not a side effect. The file itself is removed only when this store holds it.

patch.description: Alt text is the only field of a stored file worth editing; everything else describes bytes that did not change.

An email with a typo in it means the customer never hears from the shop again; an address with the wrong house number means the parcel goes to the wrong door; a payment reference is what somebody reconciles against a bank statement. None of them is a state change, and each is a field a person typed once.

Correcting an address does not move a parcel that has already gone out.
patch.summary: Correct an order's contact details and payment record

post.description: Returns the inventory. Which movement is correct depends on how far the order got: a pending order only ever reserved stock, while a confirmed one has already taken it off the shelf. An order that has shipped cannot be cancelled — that is a return.

put.description: Replaces the order's lines with the set given. A line the order already has is named by its id; one being added names a variant instead, and is priced as that variant is priced today. A line the request leaves out is removed, and an order may not be left with none — cancel it instead. Stock moves with the change: an order that has only reserved its stock has its reservation adjusted, one that has already taken the units off the shelf gives them back or takes more. The money is not settled here — the response reports the totals either side of the edit and the balance between them, and collecting or refunding it is a payment operation with its own record. An order that has shipped, been cancelled or been refunded cannot be edited.

id.description: A line the order already has. Omit for a new one.

quantity.description: Zero removes a line the order already has.

variant_id.description: The variant to add. Required when id is absent.

balance_minor.description: What the edit moved the total by: positive is owed by the customer, negative is owed to them.

200.description: The order, and what the edit changed.

put.summary: Change what is on an order

post.description: How cash on delivery is settled, and the same call a gateway module makes from its webhook. It also confirms a pending order — without that, a paid order would wait forever for a step nobody performs. Idempotent: a replayed webhook does not commit stock twice.

A correction, not a refund: it says the money never arrived and somebody marked the wrong order, so it leaves no refund behind. It moves the payment status and nothing else — a confirmed order awaiting payment is not a broken state, it is what every cash-on-delivery order already is, and un-confirming would put stock back on the shelf while the order is still live. An operator who wants the stock back cancels the order instead.

Refused on a refunded order, where money really did move, and on a cancelled one.
post.summary: Take back a payment recorded in error

post.description: Goes back through the provider that took the money. A method that cannot refund — cash on delivery, for one — reports that plainly rather than pretending. Omit the amount to refund the full total.

The order returns to shipped, and so do the fulfillments that were marked delivered with it. Nothing moved when the delivery was recorded — no stock, no money — so nothing moves back. Refused from any status but delivered.
post.summary: Take back a delivery recorded in error

parameters.description: Products carrying exactly this tag. Exact rather than case-folded so the match is answered by the index; tags are de-duplicated case-insensitively on write, so one spelling of a tag is the only spelling stored.
parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: Restrict to a category and everything nested under it. An unparseable value is an error rather than a silently ignored filter, because a filter that quietly matches everything is how a typo turns into "why is this showing the whole catalogue".
parameters.name: category_id

post.description: Options and variants may be created in the same call. For a product with no options, send `sku` and `price_minor` instead of `variants` and the single default variant is created for you.

delete.description: Order lines survive: they hold their own snapshot and their product reference is simply nulled.

get.summary: Get a product in any status

patch.description: Every field is optional; an omitted field is left alone, which is what distinguishes "not mentioned" from "set to empty".

tags.description: Replaces the whole set. Tags have no identity of their own, so "add one" is not something the engine can tell apart from a client that sent a stale list.

put.description: Replace, not merge: the caller holds the whole list. An "add" endpoint quietly re-creates a membership the operator removed in another tab, with no way for them to see that it happened. The order sent is the order stored, an unknown id rejects the whole request, and an empty list clears membership.

get.description: Read this before writing: PUT replaces the whole ordered list, so a client that attaches one file without knowing the current one silently discards the rest.
get.summary: A product's media, in display order

put.description: The body is the whole list, in order — a reorder and an add are the same request. Media already on the product keeps its position row, and with it any variant that nominated it; removing a file from the list also removes any variant's nomination of it.
put.summary: Set a product's media, in order

put.description:
Sets the whole matrix and reconciles the variants with it in one transaction — which is what an editor needs, since renaming an axis or dropping a value is a single intent that would leave the product incoherent if split across calls.

Send an option's `id` to keep it: matched by name alone, renaming "Size" to "Größe" is indistinguishable from deleting one axis and adding another, and every variant would lose its size. Omit `id` for a new axis.

A variant whose combination survives is left completely alone — price, SKU and stock included. A variant whose combination no longer exists is deleted; its order lines keep their own snapshot, so history stays readable. New combinations are created only when `generate_variants` is set.

The same value may not appear on two axes: variant options are resolved by value, so "Small" as both a Size and a Cup could not be told apart, and the request is refused rather than silently mis-resolved.

generate_variants.description: Create a variant for every combination that has none. Off by default: adding an axis should not quietly mint sellable SKUs at a guessed price.

id.description: The existing axis this replaces. Omit for a new one.

price_minor.description: Price for generated variants. Omitted copies the product's existing default.

200.description: The reconciled product, and what changed.

post.description: `options` names the value chosen on each of the product's axes, in any order. Two variants may not select the same combination — that is enforced by a unique index, not by hope.

delete.description: The last superuser cannot be removed: an admin panel nobody can sign in to is not a state an operator can click their way out of.

patch.description: Send either field, or both. Changing the password signs that operator out everywhere, because a password change is how someone responds to a compromise.
patch.summary: Change an operator's email or password

delete.description: A product must keep at least one variant: a product with nothing sellable is not a product.

patch.description: Stock is deliberately not patchable here. Inventory moves through its own endpoint so that every change is a transactional adjustment rather than a blind overwrite of a number another request may have just changed.

continue_selling.description: Take the order when the count has run out, instead of refusing it.

cost_minor.description: Send null to clear a recorded cost.

origin_country.description: Where the item was made, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

post.description: Send `adjust` to move the count by a delta (receiving stock), or `set` to replace it (a stock take). Neither may leave on-hand below the quantity already reserved for orders in flight.

put.description: `media_id` must already be on the variant's product — a variant nominates one of the product's images rather than owning a file, and attaching from here would put a picture at a position in the product's ordered list that nobody chose. Send `null` to clear. The field is required: an omitted `media_id` is a 400 rather than a guess, because guessing is how an image gets removed by a request that never mentioned it. One image per variant, enforced by a unique index.

200.description: The variant, with the image the store now holds.

put.summary: Set or clear a variant's image

post.description: Returns the cart id, which is an unguessable token. Possessing it is the authorisation — there is no account, and there never has to be.
Adding records the price now. Checkout is what makes a price authoritative, and it refuses rather than silently repricing.
post.summary: Add a variant to the cart

patch.description: A quantity of zero removes the line, which is what a stepper stepping down to nothing means.

get.description: Nested by default, because a storefront menu is nested. `?flat=1` returns the same rows depth-first, which is what an indented picker wants: every row carries `depth` and `child_count`, so a client can indent and expand without rebuilding the tree.

parameters.description: Return a depth-first flat list instead of nested children.
parameters.name: flat

200.description: The tree, or the flattened list.

get.description: Descendants are included, because that is what picking a category means: someone who asks for Apparel wants the shirts too, and a filter that returned only products filed at the exact node would show an empty page for every branch. The meta describes the products, since they are the pageable part.

200.description: The category flattened into the response, with a page of its products.

get.summary: A category and the products filed under it
List the payment methods this store accepts

post.description:
Validates the cart, reserves inventory and creates the order in one transaction, then starts payment outside it — a gateway having a slow day must not become the store having a slow day.

If a line's price changed, its product went inactive, or stock ran out, the whole checkout is refused with 409 and per-line detail; the cart is refreshed to current prices so the shopper can confirm again.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header. The same key replays the original result instead of creating a second order; if the first attempt created the order but payment initiation failed, a retry resumes payment on that same order.

parameters.description: A payment method code, such as `cod`.
parameters.name: code

201.description: The order, and what the client must do to pay.

error.message: the cart is no longer valid at these prices

409.description: The cart is no longer valid at these prices.

post.summary: Check out with a payment method

post.description: A core-owned route that hands the raw request body to the payment module, so a gateway gets a documented callback URL without the module mounting anything itself. Signature verification is the module's job.

get.description: Only collections holding at least one active product are listed. A collection that is empty, or that holds nothing but drafts, is a work in progress, and linking to it would produce an empty page.

200.description: A page of collections, in curation order.

get.summary: List the collections a storefront should show

get.description: `meta` describes the embedded products: the collection itself is a single record, and the only thing on this response a client can page through is what is in it. Products come back in the order they were curated.

200.description: The collection with a page of its active products.

get.summary: Get a collection and the active products in it

get.description: Guest checkout means there is no account to log into, so the order's access token — returned once at checkout — is the credential. A wrong token is reported as not found, so this cannot be used to discover which order numbers exist.
Only active products are visible. A draft or archived product is reported as not found rather than forbidden, because its existence is not a shopper's business.

parameters.description: Free-text match on title and description.

get.description: SKU is the catalog's stable key for import and export, which makes it the natural handle for a storefront deep link too.
get.summary: Get a product by one of its variant SKUs
Get an active product by slug

get.description: Variants are their own collection rather than a sub-path of a product: `/api/products/{id}/variants` would collide with the slug and sku lookups.

Reports that the process is running. Touches no dependency, so a database hiccup never causes an orchestrator to restart a healthy process.
Reports that this process can serve traffic, which requires the database to answer.
